einzeiler: Catching up on Gemini 3.7, Jalapeño, Qwen 3.8, drones, and the latest AI industry shifts.
kurzfassung: This episode covers recent model updates including Gemini 3.7 Flash and Grok 4.6 alongside open-source releases like Qwen 3.8. The hosts discuss major hardware developments, such as OpenAI's custom inference chip Jalapeno and Anthropic's growing semiconductor team. Additionally, they explore policy concerns including autonomous drone warfare, safety pauses, and the rising tide of AI slop online.
stichpunkte: Google released Gemini 3.7 Flash as an efficiency-focused mid-tier workhorse rather than a true frontier model.
SpaceX AI launched Grok 4.6 with a 500K context window, leveraging the Cursor acquisition for coding and agentic tasks.
Anthropic implemented invisible watermarking for text and images to comply with transparency regulations and assist in detection.
OpenAI unveiled Jalapeno, a custom inference chip promising high efficiency and heat dissipation, alongside leadership departures.
Anthropic hired Google TPU veteran Amir Selek to spearhead its internal custom silicon semiconductor program.
A Russian drone guided entirely by artificial intelligence killed three civilians in Ukraine, marking a grim milestone.
OpenAI paused reinforcement learning training for two weeks to tighten security boundaries following recent hacking incidents.
Thomson Reuters developed an in-house LLM named Thomson based on an Alibaba model to reduce external API costs.
Qwen 3.8 released a 27B dense parameter model offering high performance and local deployment capabilities.
Major platforms like LinkedIn and Spotify face a massive surge in AI-generated content, prompting new flagging features.
beschreibung:
Our 255th episode with a summary and discussion of last week's big AI news!
Recorded on 08/26/2026
Hosted by Andrey Kurenkov and Jeremie Harris
Feel free to email us your questions and feedback at andreyvkurenkov@gmail.com and/or hello@gladstone.ai
Read out our text newsletter and comment on the podcast at https://lastweekin.ai/
In this episode:
SpaceXAI released Grok 4.6 (500K context) as a post-training update aimed at long-running agents and coding, with discussion centered on how the Cursor acquisition boosts training via coding trajectories/RL environments and provides distribution despite Cursor’s market-share decline.
OpenAI shared early Jalapeno inference-chip results (better performance per watt and lower latency vs leading systems) and plans to deploy it internally by year-end, emphasizing hardware–software co-design and competitive leverage against Nvidia.
OpenAI announced security changes after an AI hacked Hugging Face, including a two-week pause on a major RL fine-tuning run while tightening internal security, raising questions about whether safety is becoming a deployment bottleneck.
Policy and misuse updates included a New York Times report of an AI-guided Russian drone strike in Ukraine believed to be the first documented fully autonomous civilian-killing incident, and a lawsuit alleging Grok was used to generate CSAM images.
